mainTopic: Cancelling a גט: what the word בטל means, which phrases cancel a גט, whether a cancelled גט can be reused, and how many people must be present.
overview: The גמרא explains that the word בטל can mean 'already void' or 'let it become void,' and each case uses the reading that actually works there: one for a גט, another for a gift. אביי adds a tradition that a שליח for a gift is like a שליח for a גט, so 'take this' (הולך) does not mean 'acquire this' (זכי). רב נחמן בר יצחק wonders whether the bare word 'void' cancels a גט, and the question ends in תיקו. רב ששת, or a ברייתא, then lists phrases that cancel a גט, like 'let it be pottery,' and phrases that do nothing, like 'it is pottery.' 'It is hereby pottery' does cancel it, just like 'it is hereby הקדש.' רב נחמן and רב ששת argue whether a cancelled גט can be used again, and the הלכה follows רב נחמן that it can. The גמרא defends this against רבי יוחנן's ruling: words can cancel words, but cancelling the שליח does not destroy the גט itself. Finally, the two argue whether cancelling a גט needs two or three people. רב נחמן begins a proof from the פרוזבול that two can be called a בית דין, and that proof continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The word 'void' has two possible meanings
steps.stepSummary: The word בטל can mean 'already void' or 'should become void'. For a גט we read it the way that works for a גט, and for a gift we read it the way that works for a gift.
steps.simpleTranslation: The word 'void' can mean two things: 'it is void already' or 'let it become void.' For a גט, he meant the meaning that works for a גט. For a gift, he meant the meaning that works for a gift.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers an earlier question: why is the same word 'void' treated differently for a גט and for a gift?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word בטל is two-sided. A husband can cancel a גט before it reaches his wife, so for a גט we read 'void' as 'let it become void from now on.' A gift cannot be cancelled once it is acquired, so for a gift we read it as 'it was void from the start.' In each case we pick the reading that actually works.

keyTerms.meaning: The word can be read two ways
Void, already cancelled
Let it become void from now on
Wording that is effective, the reading that actually works

steps.confusionAlert: The word is the same in both cases. What changes is which meaning we assume the speaker intended, based on what is legally possible in each case.

phrases.english: It has two meanings –
phrases.notes: 'It' is the word 'void' (בטל) from the earlier discussion.

phrases.english: it can mean that it is already void,
and it can mean that it should become void.
Regarding a bill of divorce, the wording
that is effective for it is what he said;
regarding a gift, the wording
that is effective for it is what he said.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers a contradiction raised just before this section, about 'void' meaning different things for a גט and for a gift.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Ambiguous wording is read differently depending on context
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The same word should carry the same meaning in both the גט case and the gift case.
steps.terutzMaskana: The word has two meanings, and each case uses the one that is legally effective there.

steps.title: An agent for a gift is like an agent for a גט
steps.stepSummary: אביי reports a tradition: a שליח delivering a gift is treated like a שליח delivering a גט. The practical result is that saying 'take' is not the same as saying 'acquire'.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: We have a tradition that an agent for a gift is like an agent for a גט. The practical difference: saying 'take it to him' is not like saying 'acquire it for him.'
steps.whatsHappening: אביי adds another comparison between a גט and a gift. A messenger told only to 'take' a gift does not acquire it for the receiver.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a גט, a husband who says 'take this to her' can still cancel it until it arrives. אביי says a gift works the same way. If the giver says 'take' (הולך), the receiver has not acquired the gift yet, so the giver can still change his mind. 'Acquire it for him' (זכי) would be different.

keyTerms.meaning: We hold, we have a received tradition
An agent delivering a gift
The practical difference that comes out of this
'Take' (deliver this)
'Acquire' (on someone's behalf)

steps.whatToRemember: Saying 'take' (הולך) is not saying 'acquire' (זכי). Until the gift arrives, the giver can still back out, just like a husband with a גט.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets a practical rule for gifts sent through messengers: whether the receiver owns the gift yet depends on the exact words the sender used.

phrases.english: Abaye said: We hold by tradition:
an agent for a gift is
like an agent for a bill of divorce;
the practical difference is that 'take'
is not like 'acquire.'
phrases.notes: So until the gift reaches the receiver, he does not own it, and the sender can still take it back.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues comparing a גט with a gift, this time about agents.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A gift agent is like a גט agent. 'Take' does not mean 'acquire', so the giver can retract before delivery.

steps.title: What if the husband says only 'void'?
steps.stepSummary: רבינא finds רב נחמן בר יצחק leaning on a door bar, wondering what the law is if the husband says just the word 'void'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא found רב נחמן בר יצחק leaning on the bar of a door, and he was wondering: if the husband says only 'void', what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a short story to bring up a new question: does the single word 'void' cancel a גט?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 1 said 'void' can mean 'already void' or 'let it become void.' If the husband says only 'void', it is unclear whether he is cancelling the גט now, which works, or just describing it as void, which does nothing. That is the doubt.

keyTerms.meaning: He found him
The bar of a door
He was asking himself, it was a question for him
What is the law?

phrases.aramaic: רָבִינָא אַשְׁכְּחֵיהּ לְרַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק
phrases.english: Ravina found Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak
leaning on the bar of a door,
and he was wondering:
if he said only 'void', what is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the word בטל from step 1 and asks about it used on its own.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the bare word 'void' cancel a גט, or is it only a description with no effect?

steps.title: The question stays unresolved
steps.stepSummary: No answer is found, so the question stays open: תיקו.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא ends the question without an answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: תיקו means we could not decide. Whether the bare word 'void' cancels a גט remains a doubt.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it stand: the question remains unresolved

phrases.english: Let it stand unresolved.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the question from step 3 without resolving it.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: It remains a doubt whether saying just 'void' cancels a גט.

steps.title: Phrases that do cancel a גט
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת, or a ברייתא according to some, lists phrases a husband can use to cancel a גט, and all of them work.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said, and some say a ברייתא taught: if the husband says 'This גט will not work', 'will not release', 'will not make her leave', 'will not send away', 'will not divorce', 'let it be pottery', or 'let it be like pottery', his words take effect.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא lists clear phrases that do cancel a גט, unlike the unclear bare word 'void'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each phrase clearly looks ahead and takes away the גט's power, so there is no doubt about what the husband means. Calling the גט 'pottery' means it is now as worthless as a broken clay shard. All of these cancel it.

keyTerms.meaning: And some say (a different source for the same teaching)
It was taught in a ברייתא
Pottery, a clay shard, something worthless
His words stand, they take effect

steps.whatToRemember: A clear, forward-looking phrase such as 'this גט will not work' or 'let it be pottery' cancels a גט. The bare word 'void' is left as a doubt.

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet said,
and some say it was taught in a baraita:
'This bill of divorce will not be effective';
'will not release'; 'will not cause her to leave';
'will not send away'; 'will not divorce';
'let it be pottery'; 'let it be like pottery' –
his words take effect.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת, וְאָמְרִי לַהּ בְּמַתְנִיתָא תָּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After leaving the bare word 'void' unresolved, the גמרא lists wordings that clearly do cancel a גט.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Phrases like 'this גט will not work' or 'let it be pottery' cancel the גט.

steps.title: Phrases that do not cancel a גט
steps.stepSummary: The list continues with phrases that do nothing. If the husband says them, the גט is still valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he says 'It has no effect,' 'it does not release,' 'it does not make her leave,' 'it does not send away,' 'it does not divorce,' 'it is pottery,' or 'it is like pottery,' he has said nothing.
steps.whatsHappening: Step 5 listed phrases that cancel a גט. Now the same source gives the opposite list: phrases that do not cancel it at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every phrase here describes the גט as not working. None of them actively cancels it. Since the גט really is valid, his description is simply untrue, so his words change nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: has an effect, works
makes her leave (from עזב, to leave)
a broken piece of clay pottery, something worthless
he said nothing; his words have no legal effect

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix the two lists. The phrases in step 5 cancel the גט. The phrases here, even though they sound negative, leave the גט fully valid.

phrases.english: "It has no effect"; "it does not release";
"it does not make her leave"; "it does not send away";
"it does not divorce"; "it is pottery";
"it is like pottery": he has said nothing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second half of the list from step 5: phrases that fail to cancel the גט.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Phrases that only describe the גט as worthless or not working do not cancel it.

steps.title: What about saying 'it is hereby pottery'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks about a phrase that falls between the two lists: 'It is hereby pottery.'
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: if he says 'It is hereby pottery,' what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new case. The husband adds the word 'hereby' to the 'pottery' phrase.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'It is pottery' does nothing because it is only a description. The word 'hereby' sounds like he is making it pottery right now, which would be an act of cancelling. So which is it?

keyTerms.meaning: a question was asked of them (the Sages)
it is hereby; wording that creates a new status
what is the law?

phrases.english: A question was asked of them:
"It is hereby pottery": what is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the phrase 'it is pottery' from step 6 and asks about a stronger form of it.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does 'it is hereby pottery' cancel the גט, or is it just a description like 'it is pottery'?

steps.title: It works, just like 'it is hereby הקדש'
steps.stepSummary: An אמורא answers that 'it is hereby pottery' is no different from 'it is hereby הקדש' or 'it is hereby הפקר', which clearly work.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said to רב אחא son of רבא, and some say רב אחא son of רבא said to רב אשי: How is this different from 'It is hereby הקדש' or 'It is hereby הפקר'?
steps.whatsHappening: The question from step 7 gets answered with a comparison. The 'hereby' wording works for the גט too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When a person says 'it is hereby הקדש' or 'it is hereby הפקר', everyone agrees he is giving the item a new status. So 'it is hereby pottery' also gives the גט a new status: it becomes worthless, and that cancels it.

keyTerms.meaning: how is it different?
property set aside for the בית המקדש
ownerless property
and some say (a second version of who said it)

steps.whatToRemember: 'It is pottery' does nothing. 'It is hereby pottery' cancels the גט.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבִינָא לְרַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרָבָא,
phrases.english: Ravina said to Rav Acha son of Rava,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמְרִי לַהּ רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרָבָא לְרַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: and some say Rav Acha son of Rava said to Rav Ashi:
How is this different from "It is hereby consecrated";
"It is hereby ownerless"?

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'It is hereby pottery' is like 'it is hereby הקדש' or 'it is hereby הפקר'. It creates a new status, so it cancels the גט.

steps.title: Can a cancelled גט be used again?
steps.stepSummary: A new question: after the husband cancels a גט, may he later divorce his wife with that same גט?
steps.simpleTranslation: Can he go back and divorce with it, or can he not go back and divorce with it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic. It asks what happens to the cancelled גט afterward.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two ways to understand the cancellation. Perhaps it only stopped this delivery, and the paper is still a good גט. Or perhaps it destroyed the גט itself, so it can never be used.

keyTerms.meaning: goes back and divorces with it (uses the same גט again)

phrases.english: Can he go back and divorce with it,
phrases.notes: This is about a גט the husband already cancelled in one of the ways that works.

phrases.english: or can he not go back and divorce with it?

steps.triggerLanguage: חוֹזֵר וּמְגָרֵשׁ בּוֹ אוֹ אֵינוֹ חוֹזֵר וּמְגָרֵשׁ בּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from how to cancel a גט to what the cancellation does to it.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does cancelling a גט destroy the document, or only stop the current attempt to deliver it?

steps.title: רב נחמן says yes, רב ששת says no
steps.stepSummary: Two אמוראים disagree. רב נחמן says the cancelled גט can be used again. רב ששת says it cannot.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: He can go back and divorce with it. רב ששת said: He cannot go back and divorce with it.
steps.whatsHappening: The question of step 9 is answered with a מחלוקת between two אמוראים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן holds that the cancellation does not ruin the document, so the גט stays usable. רב ששת holds that the cancellation makes the גט itself void, so it is finished.

keyTerms.meaning: an אמורא; here he holds the גט can be reused
an אמורא; here he holds the גט cannot be reused

phrases.aramaic: רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר: חוֹזֵר וּמְגָרֵשׁ בּוֹ;
phrases.english: Rav Nachman said: He can go back and divorce with it;

phrases.aramaic: וְרַב שֵׁשֶׁת אָמַר: אֵינוֹ חוֹזֵר וּמְגָרֵשׁ בּוֹ.
phrases.english: and Rav Sheshet said: He cannot go back and divorce with it.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר חוֹזֵר וּמְגָרֵשׁ בּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives two opposing answers to the question of step 9.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב נחמן: the גט can be reused. רב ששת: it cannot.

steps.title: The הלכה follows רב נחמן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rules like רב נחמן: a cancelled גט can be used again.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the הלכה follows רב נחמן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא decides the מחלוקת from step 10 in favor of רב נחמן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In practice, a husband who cancelled a גט may later divorce his wife with that same document. This ruling becomes the target of the very next step.

keyTerms.meaning: and the הלכה follows his view

phrases.english: And the halacha follows Rav Nachman.

steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A cancelled גט may be used again, following רב נחמן.

steps.title: Challenge from the ruling of רבי יוחנן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions the ruling like רב נחמן, because we also rule like רבי יוחנן, who said that a woman can back out of a pending קידושין.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that so? But we hold that the הלכה follows רבי יוחנן, who said: she can retract.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ruling of step 11. It points to another accepted ruling that seems to point the other way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן holds that words of retraction can fully undo an act that has not yet taken effect. If so, the husband's words of cancellation should fully undo the גט, and then it should not be usable again. That seems to clash with ruling like רב נחמן.

keyTerms.meaning: is that so? (opens a challenge)
we hold, it is established for us
she can retract (back out)

phrases.english: Is that so?!

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא קַיְימָא לַן הִלְכְתָא כְּווֹתֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן,
phrases.english: But don't we hold that the halacha follows Rabbi Yochanan,
who said: she can retract.
phrases.notes: This refers to קידושין set to take effect after thirty days. רבי יוחנן says she can back out before then.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִינִי וְהָא קַיְימָא לַן הִלְכְתָא כְּווֹתֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the ruling of step 11 by using another accepted הלכה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that the הלכה follows רב נחמן, so a cancelled גט can be reused.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוחנן shows that a spoken retraction fully undoes something before it takes effect. So the husband's cancellation should fully destroy the גט, which fits רב ששת rather than רב נחמן.

steps.title: Speech can cancel speech, but not a physical document
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the comparison to רבי יוחנן. In קידושין, her later words cancel her earlier words. Here, the husband only cancels the messenger's job, not the גט itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: How can you compare them? There, it is words against words, so new words cancel old words. Here, even if the husband cancelled the messenger's mission, did the גט itself become cancelled?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from Step 12 by showing that the two cases are not alike.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רבי יוחנן's case, the woman only agreed with words, so later words can take back that agreement. In our case, the husband's words undo the שליחות, but the גט is a written object, and words alone do not erase it. So the same גט can be sent again, and both rulings can stand.

keyTerms.meaning: How can you compare? (rejects a comparison)
Speech, spoken words
The agency, the messenger's mission
The גט itself

steps.whatToRemember: Cancelling the messenger is not the same as destroying the גט. Because of that, the ruling like רב נחמן does not clash with רבי יוחנן.

phrases.english: How can these be compared?!
There, it is speech and speech,
phrases.notes: "There" means רבי יוחנן's case of the woman backing out of קידושין.

phrases.english: so speech comes and cancels speech;
but here, granted that he cancelled
the mission of the messenger,
is the גט itself cancelled?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the challenge of Step 12 by showing that the two cases are different.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The comparison between a woman backing out of קידושין and a husband cancelling a גט
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The comparison ignores that a גט is a physical document, while her consent was only speech.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The ruling like רב נחמן stands: a cancelled גט can be used again.

steps.title: How many people must be present to cancel a גט?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה, which says that at first the husband would make a court to cancel the גט. It then asks how many people are needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: at first he would make a court. It was asked: in front of how many people does he cancel it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic by quoting the משנה and asking a question. This sets up the disagreement in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said the husband used to cancel the גט in front of a בית דין, but it did not say how many people that takes. The גמרא wants the exact number.

keyTerms.meaning: At first, in earlier times
It was stated (introduces a disagreement between אמוראים)
He cancels it

phrases.english: At first he would make [a court].
phrases.notes: These are the משנה's words. It means he would gather a בית דין somewhere else to cancel the גט.

phrases.english: It was stated:
In front of how many does he cancel it?

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּרִאשׁוֹנָה הָיָה עוֹשֶׂה. אִיתְּמַר, בִּפְנֵי כַּמָּה הוּא מְבַטְּלוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the topic of reusing a גט and goes back to the next line of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How many people make up the 'court' in front of which the husband cancels the גט

steps.title: רב נחמן says two, רב ששת says three
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן says two people are enough. רב ששת says three are needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: in front of two. רב ששת said: in front of three.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים give different answers to the question of how many people are needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The disagreement is about the minimum number of people. Three is a normal בית דין. Two is a smaller group, so רב נחמן's view is the more lenient one.

keyTerms.meaning: In front of two people
In front of three people

phrases.english: רב נחמן said: in front of two;
רב ששת said: in front of three.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר: בִּפְנֵי שְׁנַיִם; רַב שֵׁשֶׁת אָמַר: בִּפְנֵי שְׁלֹשָׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 14 with two opinions.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב נחמן: two people. רב ששת: three people.

steps.title: Why each one holds his view
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת says three because the משנה uses the word 'בית דין', which normally means three. רב נחמן says two can also be called a בית דין.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת says three because the משנה says 'בית דין'. רב נחמן says two because two people are also called a 'בית דין'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the reason behind each opinion. Both opinions are built on the same word in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both agree the משנה requires a 'בית דין'. They disagree about what that word means. רב ששת reads it as a normal court of three, and רב נחמן holds that two people can also be called a בית דין.

keyTerms.meaning: A court
It (the משנה) teaches
Calls them

phrases.english: רב ששת said in front of three,
because the משנה teaches 'a court'.
And רב נחמן said in front of two,

phrases.aramaic: לְבֵי תְרֵי נָמֵי ״בֵּית דִּין״ קָרֵי לְהוּ.
phrases.english: because a pair of two is also called 'a court'.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב שֵׁשֶׁת אָמַר בִּפְנֵי שְׁלֹשָׁה – ״בֵּית דִּין״ קָתָנֵי

steps.mimraCoreRuling: The disagreement depends on whether the word 'בית דין' can include a group of two.

steps.title: רב נחמן begins his proof from the פרוזבול
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן starts to prove that two people can be called a בית דין, by quoting the formula of the פרוזבול.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: From where do I say this? As we learned in a משנה: 'I hand over to you...'
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן begins bringing a source for his view. The quote, and the proof, continue on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן wants to show from a משנה that two people are called a בית דין. He opens the פרוזבול formula, where a lender hands his debts over to the court. The proof itself will come from how that formula continues.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do I say this?

phrases.english: רב נחמן said:
From where do I say this?
As we learned: 'I hand over to you, in front of you,'
phrases.notes: This is the start of the פרוזבול formula from the משנה in שביעית 10:4. The quote continues on the next amud.
